title: Hearing Joe Oliver in New Orleans: picnics, wind and the break
summary: Oliver drew away Dominique's picnic crowd at the lake pavilions, had long wind, and his blues break snagged Louis and Dominique.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, well, somewhere he died. Savannah, Georgia. But Joe's a good musician. He played a few parades with many parades. The same King Oliver.
Yeah.
Yeah, he's on a lot.
Do you remember if he was very good in those old days in New Orleans?
Very good.
Very good. You heard him first.
Heard him first. I played a picnic right alongside of Joe. He took all my people away from me. Yes, indeed. You know, I had them pavilions on the lake.
Oh, yeah.
They played picnics on the pavilions. People dancing like that. Well, Joe was right next to me. I said, you're about a block away from me?
Yeah.
He took all my folks away from me.
They all went over to hear him.
Yeah, we had to close up the place.
So we did that.
Played a lot of corners. Joe played a lot of corners. And he had longer wind than any man I've seen in the car.
More wind?
More wind.
Yeah.
Could blow a long.
Yeah.
Could blow a long time. Longer. Longer than Louis. Because when he came with that blues he had there, he had a, I think it's a 12 or 16-bar break.
Oh, yeah. Snagging.
That's the one that throwed us. Snagging.
Snagging.
It snagged Louis and I. With the look.
It throws us. Was his tone more powerful than Louis? No. Than Louis and other players? No.
He didn't have the tones more powerful than Louis. It made them more powerful than I, but he had a nice tone.
